items.question: Who becomes free from bondage after six months of practice while wearing an ochre robe?
premises: Six months of practice frees one from bondage.
The practitioner wears an ochre robe.
items.inference: The verse links six months of practice with freedom from bondage for the ochre-robed practitioner.
uncertainties: Exact grammatical case of ṣaṇmāsād is inferred.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months in an ochre robe becomes free from bondage.

items.question: What union occurs for one freed from all diseases with yogis?
premises: The person is freed from all diseases.
He joins yogis in union.
items.inference: Freedom from disease leads to union with yogis.
uncertainties: saha+melakam may be accusative object or adverbial.
items.plain_english: One freed from all diseases attains union together with yogis.

items.question: What practice of the soul has been told to Bhairavi?
premises: This practice of the soul is told.
It is told to you, Bhairavi.
items.inference: The verse states that the soul-practice has been communicated to Bhairavi.
uncertainties: te appears twice with possibly different referents.
items.plain_english: This practice of the soul has been told to you, O Bhairavi.

items.question: To whom should the teaching be given when the mind is resolved?
premises: It is to be given to one endowed with all states.
It is given to one of resolved mind.
items.inference: The verse restricts giving to a qualified and resolved recipient.
uncertainties: dātavyaṃ may imply an unstated object.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one endowed with all states and of resolved mind.

items.question: Why should the kaula essence not be given to yoginis?
premises: The kaula essence is not to be given.
It concerns origin among yoginis.
items.inference: The verse withholds the kaula essence from yoginis.
uncertainties: sambhavam may modify sāraṃ or yoginīnām.
items.plain_english: The kaula essence, arising among yoginis, should not be given.

items.question: How is the pure body struck by the veil of ignorance?
premises: Today my pure body is struck.
It is struck by the veil of ignorance.
items.inference: The verse describes the body as pure yet affected by ignorance.
uncertainties: me may be dative rather than genitive.
items.plain_english: Today my pure body is struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious deception of time does one wish to hear now?
premises: Now I wish to hear.
I wish to hear the auspicious deception of time.
items.inference: The verse expresses a desire to hear time's auspicious deception.
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ may mean trickery or avoidance.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious deception of time.

items.question: How is death destroyed according to the teaching?
premises: I tell without doubt.
Death is destroyed as stated.
items.inference: The verse assures that death is destroyed by the described method.
uncertainties: The exact method is not named in this verse.
items.plain_english: I tell you without doubt: death is destroyed.

items.question: What happens to even a wise one burning at the tip of nectar with essence of juice?
premises: Even a wise one is burning.
The burning occurs at the tip of nectar with essence of juice.
items.inference: The verse warns that wisdom does not prevent burning in this nectar practice.
items.plain_english: Even a wise one burns at the tip of nectar with the essence of juice.

items.question: How should air be drunk slowly at the root of tongue and palate?
premises: Air is placed at the root of tongue and palate.
It should be drunk slowly.
items.inference: The verse prescribes slow drinking of air at that bodily location.
uncertainties: chanaiḥ may modify kṛtvā or pibec.
items.plain_english: Having placed air at the root of tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.

items.question: What is destroyed when the practice is done for one year?
premises: The practice is done for one year.
Old age and death are destroyed.
items.inference: One year of practice destroys old age and death.
uncertainties: yadā+abhyastañ may be locative or nominative.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: Why does poison not enter the body even when bitten by great serpents?
premises: Poison does not enter the body.
This holds even when bitten by great serpents.
items.inference: The verse claims immunity to serpent poison in the body.
uncertainties: daṃśito may modify the subject or an implied person.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
